result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.delete_nodes_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Delete all selected nodes and their incident edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1826-L1917){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.delete_nodes_ws() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Delete selected nodes](/assets/graphs/delete-nodes-ws.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a six-node graph with nodes B and E selected in the accent color. Right: B and E are gone along with all five of their incident edges, shown as dashed outlines; only A, C, D, F and the edges A–D and C–F remain." width="100%"} Removes nodes in the current selection from the graph, along with all edges connected to those nodes. Updates selection state and removes the selected nodes from the graph structure. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Deletion acts on whatever nodes are currently selected, so select the nodes to remove first. Here, the two middle nodes of a five-node path are selected and deleted, leaving three nodes behind: ::: {#61e2c793 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) # path: 0-1-2-3-4 node_ids = list(graph.get_node_ids()) graph.select_nodes_by_id([node_ids[2], node_ids[3]]) graph.delete_nodes_ws() graph.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Because deleting a node also removes its incident edges, the path above is left with only the edge connecting the first two surviving nodes: ::: {#a3e4225a .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(5) node_ids = list(graph.get_node_ids()) graph.select_nodes_by_id([node_ids[2], node_ids[3]]) graph.delete_nodes_ws() graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Selection also accepts a predicate, which is convenient for deleting nodes based on their attributes rather than their IDs: ::: {#3d5eb7f5 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A", value=10) .add_node(label="B", value=25) .add_node(label="C", value=30) .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") ) graph.select_nodes(lambda n: n.attributes.get("value", 0) > 20) graph.delete_nodes_ws() # only "A", whose value is 20 or below, survives graph.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 1 ``` ::: :::
